resources.string: The dip at the top of the sternum lies between the points where the clavicles meet the chest.
The broad upper part meets the two clavicles and the first costal cartilages.
The ridge where the manubrium meets the body sits at the level of the second costal cartilage.
The long middle part provides attachment points for the costal cartilages along both sides.
The small lower tip is initially cartilaginous and can ossify with age. Its shape varies from person to person.
Each of the four fingers has three phalanges, joined by joints that let the finger bend.
The thumb has two phalanges rather than three. Its broad movement also depends on the joint at the base of its metacarpal.
Five metacarpal bones link the wrist to the digits and form the framework of the palm.
Eight small bones in two rows form the base of the hand. Some meet the radius at the wrist.
This small round carpal sits on the palm side of the triquetrum near the little-finger edge.
